haiku-low.q1: Three consecutive breaches (error rate above 2%, at least 500 requests in the 5-minute window) with no open incident for that service and rule.
haiku-low.q2: Each further breach is recorded as a breach event on the open incident for context. It never pages anyone.
haiku-low.q3: Ten consecutive clear evaluations (rate below 1%, 10 minutes) resolve it and cancel pending timers. A later breach starts a new streak; three are needed to open a new incident.
haiku-low.q4: Level 1 pages when the incident opens. If unacknowledged after 5 minutes, level 2 is paged; if still unacknowledged after another 5 minutes, level 3 is paged, the last level.
haiku-low.q5: SMS is sent right away in the same dispatch with the same idempotency key. Failed sends retry with backoff and never change the escalation timer.
haiku-low.q6: Each responder recorded on a page row gets a resolved notice, push then SMS on failure. Pending escalation timers are cancelled.
haiku-low.q7: In the rule_state table's breach_streak and clear_streak columns. A window that is neither breach nor clear resets both; a different kind of evaluation ends the other streak.
haiku-low.q8: Each evaluator takes a row lock on rule_state. The first to commit sets last_tick; the second sees it, rolls back and skips. A partial unique index also refuses a second open incident.
haiku-low.q9: A timer due 5 minutes after its page commits. It pages the next level only if the incident is still open, unacknowledged and at the expected level; otherwise it does nothing.
haiku-low.q10: The paging provider calls the ack webhook with page and event IDs. If open and unacknowledged, it sets acked_by and acked_at and cancels pending escalation timers. Repeated event IDs are ignored.
haiku-low.q11: The responder is looked up at send time, not when the incident opened, so mid-incident handovers such as 09:00 are respected. If the on-call service is down, the last cached roster is used.
haiku-low.q12: Each page row stores the target person paged at each level, and resolved notices go to the people recorded there. Each page row gets its own RESOLVED outbox message.

sonnet.q1: 3 consecutive breaches (rate above 2% with at least 500 requests in the trailing 5-minute window, evaluated each 60 s tick), and no open incident already exists for that service and rule (the partial unique index also enforces one open incident).
sonnet.q2: No new incident or page is created. Each breaching evaluation is recorded as a breach_events row on the open incident, for context only, and never pages anyone.
sonnet.q3: 10 consecutive clear evaluations (rate below 1%, any traffic volume; 10 minutes) while an incident is open. The incident is marked resolved and pending timers are cancelled. What happens on a later breach: the document does not say explicitly; by the rules, with no open incident, 3 new consecutive breaches would open a new incident.
sonnet.q4: Level 1 (primary on-call) is paged when the incident opens. If still unacknowledged 5 minutes after that page's commit, level 2 (secondary) is paged. If still unacknowledged 5 minutes after that, level 3 (engineering manager) is paged. No timer after level 3.
sonnet.q5: Failed sends are retried with backoff and never change the timer. If push fails, SMS is sent immediately in the same dispatch with the same idempotency key (a timed-out push may still have been delivered, so both can arrive). The escalation timer is unaffected, since it starts at commit of the page row.
sonnet.q6: A RESOLVED notice is written to the outbox for each page row, so everyone recorded as paged is notified (push, then SMS on failure; retried if it fails). Pending escalation timers are cancelled when the incident is resolved.
sonnet.q7: In the state database, in the rule_state table (one row per service and rule: breach_streak and clear_streak). A window that is neither breach nor clear resets both streaks; a window below 500 requests is not a breach and resets the breach streak. A zero-request window changes no streaks. Metrics query failure also changes no streaks.
sonnet.q8: Each evaluator takes a SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row lock on the rule_state row in a transaction. The first to commit sets last_tick to the tick time; the second then sees last_tick already equals the tick, rolls back and skips. A partial unique index allows only one open incident per service and rule as a second guard.
sonnet.q9: A due escalation timer row (due_at reached), claimed by the dispatcher with SKIP LOCKED. It locks the incident and checks that it is still open, not acknowledged, and its level equals the timer's expected_level. If all pass, it raises the level by one, writes a page row and outbox PAGE, and creates a new timer (only if the new level is 2). If any check fails, the timer is marked done and nothing is paged.
sonnet.q10: The responder taps Acknowledge in the paging provider app; the provider calls the ack webhook with page id and event id. The webhook locks the incident and, if open and not acked, sets acked_by and acked_at, cancels pending escalation timers, and returns 200. Repeated event IDs (processed_events) change nothing. Even if timers were not cancelled, the timer's not-acknowledged check stops escalation.
sonnet.q11: At send time, by the dispatcher asking the on-call service who is primary for the service now (the target is stored on the page row then), not when the incident opens. This respects the 09:00 daily handover mid-incident.
sonnet.q12: From the pages table: the resolved notices go to the targets recorded on the page rows for that incident. At resolution an outbox RESOLVED notice is written for each page row.
